title: Creator content preferred in AI recommendations: Here's what the numbers say
tldr: Over half of consumers prefer AI recommendations informed by creators, per new IAB findings. Signals a shift in how people trust AI-surfaced content and what that means for creator strategy.
why_fresh: new data on AI + creator trust
angle: Why human-created content beats synthetic in the AI answer era — and how to build for citation-worthiness.

title: "An astonishing theft of unprecedented proportions": Court records show what Microsoft and OpenAI actually thought about AI training
tldr: Newly unsealed filings reveal Microsoft/OpenAI internally described their data scraping as massive theft and a web-damaging 'doom loop.' Damning evidence for the content-value and copyright debate.
angle: What the 'doom loop' admission means for publishers and the future economics of original content.

title: Future of Marketing Briefing: Creators are learning to pitch AEO, not just audiences
tldr: Creators now sell brands on getting cited by AI answer engines, not just reach. A concrete new pitch dynamic reshaping creator-brand deals.
angle: 'I got cited' as the new creator KPI — how AEO is rewriting influencer value.

title: I Tracked 13,184 AI Citations Across 4 LLMs: Here's What I Learned
tldr: A large-scale hands-on study of what sources LLMs actually cite, with practical takeaways for content visibility. Rare original data on AI citation behavior.
angle: Reverse-engineering LLM citations: what content actually gets surfaced, and how to earn it.

title: The Scoop: Warren Buffett says goodbye in very human signoff
tldr: Buffett's plainspoken, human farewell as Berkshire chairman is a case study in authentic executive communication. Contrast to polished corporate messaging.
angle: The power of a human signoff: what Buffett's farewell teaches about executive positioning.

title: Собеседования снова в офисе? Как ИИ ломает онлайн-наем
tldr: Candidates use $20 AI teleprompters on video calls, pushing big tech back to in-person interviews. A sharp look at how AI is breaking a trusted digital format.
angle: When AI erodes trust in digital formats, humans revert to in-person — a lesson for content authenticity.

title: Advertising is coming to AI chatbots — and it could influence the answers you get
tldr: Ads are entering AI chatbots, potentially shaping the answers users receive. Raises trust, transparency and content-integrity questions for brands.
angle: Native ads inside AI answers: the next credibility battleground for brands.

title: Instacart enlists icons like Shrek, Scooby-Doo to market AI assistant
tldr: Instacart uses nostalgic characters to humanize and explain its Clementine AI assistant. A concrete campaign breakdown of making AI relatable through storytelling.
angle: Using nostalgia and beloved characters to make AI products feel human.

title: Five independent climate journalists are teaming up with a "pop-up newsroom"
tldr: Five solo climate journalists are forming a temporary collective to regain newsroom collaboration. A new model for independent, sustainable journalism.
angle: Pop-up newsrooms: a template for freelancers and content teams to collaborate without a fixed org.

title: OpenAI is turning ChatGPT ads into conversations
tldr: OpenAI is developing conversational ad formats within ChatGPT, a fundamental shift in how brand messaging appears in AI. Big implications for content and media strategy.
angle: Conversational ads: what happens to brand storytelling when the ad is a dialogue.

title: For some ad campaigns, brands are borrowing from classic TV
tldr: Brands are mining nostalgic classic-TV aesthetics for current campaigns. A trend piece on how retro formats drive emotional resonance.
angle: Nostalgia as a content strategy: why retro formats keep winning attention.

title: Media as a distinctive brand asset
tldr: Argues media placements can build brand associations just like logos and jingles. A fresh reframe of owned/earned media as a distinctive asset.
angle: Treating your media choices as a distinctive brand asset, not just distribution.

title: Бренды и агентства: почему старый формат сотрудничества зашел в тупик
tldr: KITCHEN and RLVNT research on why beautiful creative without data no longer works and what clients and agencies must agree before starting. Concrete industry-relationship shift.
angle: Data-first creative: the new rules of the brand-agency contract.

title: What crisis communication framework does your team actually need?
tldr: Argues there's no one-size-fits-all crisis playbook and offers how to tailor frameworks by risk profile. Practical guidance for comms leaders.
angle: Why generic crisis playbooks fail and how to build a risk-specific one.
